item.description: Paperclip is an open-source MIT-licensed app for managing AI agents at work, with a quickstart, docs, and Discord community. It helps teams that need one place to supervise many agents in daily workflows. Developers running agents in production may want to give it a look.

item.title: [juejin] Cursor 转 Codex 大半个月，聊聊我的真实感受
item.description: A developer shares impressions after roughly half a month of switching from Cursor to Codex. Cursor was what first made AI coding feel striking, the author says, while Codex feels less like a coding assistant and more like a genuine super-agent, closer to the next stage of the form. Useful for anyone weighing a move from Cursor to Codex.

item.title: [infoq] Claude Opus 5.5 发布：一天内迁移 68 万行代码，单任务成本比 GPT-6 Astra 便宜 80%
item.description: Anthropic released Claude Opus 5.5, the first model in its Claude 5.5 line, shifting focus from scaling to better coding, computer use and knowledge work while cutting typical task cost about 40% versus Opus 5. The company says an early tester migrated 680,000 lines of code in under a day, and that on FrontierCode each task costs roughly 20% of GPT-6 Astra's. Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 are coming next.

item.title: [v2ex] [OpenAI] 这下得给个重置吧！ unexpected status 401 Unauthorized: Incorrect API key provided
item.description: A V2EX user hit "401 Unauthorized: Incorrect API key provided" from OpenAI, assumed their account had been banned, then found on status.openai.com that the service was broadly down. It is a reminder that a 401 can originate upstream rather than from a bad key, so check the status page before rotating credentials or rebuilding clients.

The poster argues many vpngate.net endpoints are scarce, clean residential IPs, though the reliability of these public nodes is left for users to verify themselves.

item.title: [juejin] 面试官问你：“AI 能写 80% 的代码了，公司为什么还需要你？”
item.description: A Juejin article tackles the interview question "AI can already write 80% of the code, so why does the company still need you?" It contrasts 2026 interviews with those two years ago, when candidates hand-wrote a Promise or explained React Fiber internals; today interviewers assume AI use and probe something else. Useful for developers preparing for interviews or doing the hiring, though the supplied excerpt cuts off before the full argument.

item.title: [github_trending] vectorize-io/hindsight
item.description: Hindsight is an open-source agent-memory project from vectorize-io, pitched as memory that learns. It ships a Python package (hindsight-api), an npm client, docs, a cookbook, a benchmark site and an arXiv paper (2512.12818), plus a hosted Hindsight Cloud. Developers who want a persistent memory layer for agents without building one from scratch can check its benchmarks first.

item.title: [infoq] 从“单目感知”到“多视角立体对齐”：PrismAlign 重新定义文档结构化提取的精度上限
item.description: PrismAlign, a Huawei paper accepted to EMNLP Industry Track 2026, runs several VLM views over the same document layout and reconciles their outputs with a Bayesian decision layer to curb table-OCR hallucinations. It targets systematic failures such as invented cells, flattened multi-level headers and misread punctuation in nested, rotated or gridline-free tables, and is aimed at teams building document extraction pipelines.

item.title: [infoq] 人人都在造世界模型，HappyWorld‑Bench 试着给出一张统一考卷
item.description: Released at the Yunqi conference, HappyWorld-Bench proposes a shared exam for world models rather than debating definitions, splitting capability into representation, prediction and interaction and grading models across six levels, W1 to W6. It targets a field where Genie 3-style video world generators, 3D reconstruction efforts like Marble and embodied models each set their own rules and claim the lead.

item.title: [v2ex] [程序员] [开源] 基于 Edge TTS 的语音合成服务，兼容 OpenAI 音频接口
item.description: DejavuMoe open-sourced edgeTTS, which wraps the free Edge TTS endpoint in a service compatible with OpenAI's /v1/audio/speech API, so existing clients only need a new base URL. It handles long text through built-in chunking and audio stream stitching, supports voice mapping and parameter tuning, and ships a one-command Docker image.

item.title: [infoq] 29 小时攻破浏览器，GPT-6 Astra 成为 OpenAI 首个“严重级”模型
item.description: OpenAI rated GPT-6 Astra's cybersecurity capability as "severe" under its Preparedness Framework, the first model to cross that threshold, and Microsoft said the same day that it is available in Foundry Models. In expert-supervised tests, Astra built a browser sandbox-escape chain in 29 hours, adapted it to the official stable build in 12 more, and produced a working kernel local privilege escalation in 12 hours.

F-Droid distributes free and open-source Android apps, so FOSS users and maintainers are the main audience.

item.title: [infoq] 利用 AI 搭建内部开发者平台
item.description: Speaking at KubeCon Europe, Whitney Lee and Viktor Farcic argued that agents are becoming the new internal developer platform, replacing tools like Backstage: an agent takes a developer's request, enriches it with context pulled via semantic search over Git repos, Slack threads, Jira tickets and Zoom recordings, then passes it to an LLM that either answers or calls tools. Farcic stressed guardrails to block or approve agent actions, and using OpenTelemetry's GenAI semantic conventions to capture

item.title: [infoq] 60 万行巨石应用 AI 重构的可验证交付工程｜QCon上海
item.description: At QCon Shanghai on October 22–24, Ant Group engineer Jiang Yu will present "Verifiable Delivery Engineering for AI Refactoring of a 600k-Line Monolith," drawn from Alipay's life-bill payment system: about 600,000 lines of Java and over 600 interfaces rewritten across languages. Rather than migrating code, the project migrates behavior — PERS modeling and Case-Forge generate scenarios, and Bubble replays them to verify behavioral differences and support staged traffic cutover.

item.title: [producthunt] Naise AI
item.description: Naise AI is a new Product Hunt listing for autonomous marketing agents, described in one line as agents that "actually execute" rather than just advise. It's aimed at teams that want AI to carry marketing work through to completion; beyond that tagline, no further product details are available.

item.title: [v2ex] [分享创造] Que —— 让 Agent 排队来找你
item.description: Que funnels pending agent sessions into a single queue, so agents wait in line for your attention instead of you switching between windows to find who is blocked. It lets you drive mainstream CLI agents from terminal cards and surfaces external agent sessions as notification cards. The tool is open-sourced on GitHub.

item.title: [infoq] WSO2 发布 Agent Manager，企业寻求应对日益严重的 AI Agent 泛滥问题
item.description: WSO2 has released Agent Manager, separating agent governance from agent logic so enterprises can apply uniform controls regardless of the underlying model, framework, or runtime. It offers verifiable agent identities, RBAC, delegation and revocation, 40-plus built-in controls such as PII redaction and rate limiting, plus MCP governance and a Kubernetes-native sandbox runtime. It entered beta in June 2026 and supports LangChain, CrewAI, Bedrock and similar stacks.

item.title: [github_trending] google/ax
item.description: AX is Google's open-source declarative orchestration runtime for agents, pitched as a high-throughput scheduler that can run billions of autonomous agent tasks per cluster. It uses Agent Substrate for sandboxed execution and feels much like Kubernetes: you declare Workspace and Task resources in YAML with git repos and goals, apply them, and can ssh into the sandbox. The project is pre-stable, with breaking changes expected before a stable release.

item.title: [producthunt] Scholé Learn by Building
item.description: Scholé is a learning product launched on Product Hunt that centers on learning by building, with the tagline that studying should amount to more than "click next." The listing offers nothing further about format, subject matter or pricing, so it is mainly a pointer for people looking for hands-on, project-based learning tools.

item.title: [infoq] GPT-6猛砍价，Opus 5.5忙“变好用”：模型价格战，已经不能只看API定价
item.description: On September 23, OpenAI and Anthropic shipped new models roughly an hour apart: GPT-6 Sol for professional work, coding and complex agent tasks, the cheaper GPT-6 Luna, and Claude Opus 5.5, which adds Communication as an upgrade focus. Sol's API input price fell from $4 to $2 per million tokens and output from $20 to $10, with Luna halved again — the race is shifting from token prices to the cost of completing a task.

item.title: [v2ex] [程序员] 独立开发产品无收入，有必要买 Claude Max 吗
item.description: An independent developer paying $20 each for Codex and Claude says Codex runs out of quota before finishing tasks while Claude holds up better, yet $40 a month still leaves progress slow. He is weighing a jump to Claude Max to ship faster, but hesitates because his products earn nothing and, as he puts it, there are more products than users. He is asking for advice.

item.title: [producthunt] Floot MCP

item.title: [github_trending] rohitg00/ai-engineering-from-scratch
item.description: ai-engineering-from-scratch is a self-study repository for AI engineering, positioned as a reference manual and showing 523 lessons in its README. It is MIT-licensed and provides translated landing pages in Spanish, French, Japanese and more; English is canonical, and lesson pages are machine-translated on the translations branch. Aimed at developers who want to learn, build, and ship AI projects.

item.title: [juejin] Vibe Coding 时代：Vue 消失了还是 React 太强？
item.description: This article explores the shifting status of Vue and React in the era of Vibe Coding, where AI-assisted development is driven by mood and flow. The author analyzes why some believe Vue is fading while React grows stronger, noting that AI coding tools may favor React's ecosystem. It prompts readers to think about how frontend developers should choose their stack and whether Vue truly faces an existential threat as AI-assisted coding becomes mainstream.

item.title: [github_trending] dream-num/univer

It offers a plugin architecture, Canvas-based rendering, a formula engine, and one Facade API that runs both in the browser and on Node.js. Developers embedding spreadsheet or document features into their own products are the intended users.

item.title: [github_trending] mattpocock/skills
item.description: Matt Pocock open-sourced his personal AI agent skills in mattpocock/skills, taken from his own .agents directory and used for real engineering, not vibe coding. Unlike frameworks like GSD, BMAD, or Spec-Kit that own the whole process, these skills are deliberately small, adaptable, composable, and model-agnostic, giving developers more control. He encourages hacking on them and making them your own.

item.description: A long-form Juejin post lays out best practices for Codex, arguing that you should first understand how the model behaves before putting it to work. It walks through familiar failure modes: strong models producing unstable results, big swings when a task is rephrased, drift as conversations get longer, and more features than most people know how to use.

It is aimed at backend developers choosing an authentication strategy and wondering where JWTs actually fall short in production.

item.description: NVIDIA has open-sourced Model Optimizer (ModelOpt), a single library bundling quantization, pruning, NAS, distillation, speculative decoding and sparsity, with Hugging Face, PyTorch and ONNX inputs under an Apache 2.0 license. It ships as the nvidia-modelopt package on PyPI and targets developers who need to compress deep learning models before deployment.

item.title: [github_trending] pbakaus/impeccable
